description: This case study is the Defense Use Case report on the cyber attack against the Ukrainian power grid of 23 December 2015, written by SANS ICS analysts with the electricity sector's information sharing centre and dated 18 March 2016. It summarises the incidents at three regional distribution companies, including Kyivoblenergo, describes the attacker's tactics such as spear phishing, BlackEnergy 3 malware, credential harvesting and hijacking of SCADA operator interfaces, maps the attack onto the ICS Cyber Kill Chain in two stages, and lists passive and active defence lessons and recommendations. It states that outages affected up to 225,000 customers for several hours, the first publicly acknowledged cyber incidents to cause power outages, and evaluates the credibility of the public information in an appendix. Access: free 30-page PDF released as TLP White for unrestricted distribution subject to copyright; copies are held by the National Security Archive. Coverage is one attack on Ukrainian distribution networks. Caveats: it relies on public information and analysis, not a full forensic record, and the chain of events is limited to what was public in 2016. It suits cascading failure and resilience studies of cyber-physical attacks on power systems, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: The analysis finds that the attackers used spear phishing and BlackEnergy 3 malware to enter the IT networks, harvested credentials, reached the industrial control networks and operated the SCADA human machine interfaces, affecting up to 225,000 customers in three distribution territories for several hours. It rates the event low on a macro scale but critical to the companies, maps the attack to the ICS cyber kill chain, and offers passive and active defence lessons and recommendations.
